evidence: Quake III movement parameters keep ground acceleration, air acceleration, water acceleration, and friction as separate tuning knobs instead of one generic movement scalar.
Quake III friction is separate from acceleration and distinguishes ground, water, flight, and spectator slowdown, which is important for momentum-preserving movement.
QuakeWorld ramp-jump handling can raise max ground speed on slopes, which suggests slope-driven launch tech is part of the movement language.
QuakeWorld jump checks use jump-held gating and a discrete upward impulse, preventing pogoing while keeping jump timing skillful.
QuakeWorld air move is its own path and combines command input with acceleration after friction, which is the right pattern for touch-based air steering.
